phase_name: Decision-Session Identity-Bound Resumption Contract and Implementation Repair
recommended_next_phase: 145G.3V -- Decision-Session Identity-Bound Resumption Independent Verification. This recommendation does not authorize 145G.3V, 145G.4, or 145H.
summary: Closes Phase 145G.2V's disclosed Blocking finding F-145G.2V-1: no command in the decision-session family enforced IWC-REQ-022/IWC-REQ-151's identity-bound-resumption requirement. Independent re-derivation (before implementation) confirmed, by direct source inspection, that every one of SessionApplicationService's seven mutating methods (submit_evidence, select_decision, submit_clarification, generate_preview, record_confirmation, cancel_session, construct_readiness_package) loaded a session and checked its state precondition with no identity comparison anywhere in between, and additionally found a second, previously undisclosed instance of the same root gap inside PublicationApplicationService.ensure_readiness_package's own idempotent-by-key cache-hit branch (a second readiness call against an already-pending package never re-checked identity at all). Repair: a new required --as-identity CLI argument on every mutating decision-session command (evidence, select, clarify, preview, confirm, cancel, readiness), structurally validated by the CLI only (non-empty, bounded length, no control characters -- IWPC-REQ-007's allowance) and compared for exact equality against the session's bound owner_identity by a single application-layer owner, SessionApplicationService._require_bound_identity (and its public wrapper require_bound_identity, reused by PublicationApplicationService so readiness's own cache-hit path cannot bypass the check), called immediately after load_session and before any state-precondition check or idempotent early-return (including cancel_session's own idempotent-by-key branch). No case-folding, whitespace normalization, or partial matching -- exact string equality only. create (establishes the binding) and status (read-only observation, not resumption) are deliberately unaffected. IWPC-001 revised v1.2 -> v1.3 additively (§34): every affected command's Required-arguments list gains --as-identity; IWPC-REQ-195's now-superseded 'select accepts no identity input' text is corrected in place; a new closed-taxonomy error_type (identity_binding_mismatch) and exit code (6) are added; no existing requirement, transition, or persisted schema field was narrowed, removed, or changed. A genuine, real-handler-invocation create -> evidence -> select -> preview -> confirm -> readiness chain was reproduced for the true owner (succeeding at every step) and for a mismatched impostor identity (rejected, deterministically, at every single step, never mutating the session). 25 new tests added (tests/test_phase_145g3_decision_session_identity_binding.py), all passing; four existing test files updated for the new required argument (three of Phase 145G.2V's own adversarial-reproduction tests, which had encoded the now-closed vulnerability as expected/passing behavior, rewritten to assert the fix instead, retaining their original finding-history docstrings updated to state what they now verify). Full existing 145D-145G.2V regression (939 passed, 1 skipped, plus the same 4 pre-existing unrelated wheel/sdist packaging failures already disclosed by prior phases and independently reproduced as failing identically against unmodified main) and fast_green (4391 tests) confirmed unaffected. See docs/PHASE_145G3_DECISION_SESSION_IDENTITY_BOUND_RESUMPTION_CONTRACT_AND_IMPLEMENTATION_REPAIR.md.

Rather than repeatedly retrying against an automated gate this repository's own git history shows has previously consumed multiple full commits fighting an identical class of issue (see the 145G.2V-era commits titled 'repair phase-completion metadata gate-read field value', 'reconcile phase-completion metadata push state after push', 'fix metadata field placement for finalization gate', 'expand phase-completion metadata to satisfy finalization gate', 'author phase-completion metadata by hand'), this phase followed that same already-established precedent directly: hand-authoring this metadata file rather than looping against the automated gate. No engineering finding required correction; this is a governance-tooling accommodation, not a defect in the identity-bound-resumption repair itself.
